Job.JobTitle: Oasis Charter School- Food Service Substitute
Job.JobDescription:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

Under the general supervision of the Lead Food Service Worker, the Substitute Food Service Worker is responsible for preparing and serving food to students and staff, maintaining a clean and sanitary work environment, and stocking of inventory and supplies. 

Individual(s) assigned to this classification must report to work per their assigned schedule.

Background Screening Requirement:
Florida law requires all school personnel to undergo a Level 2 background screening through the Florida Department of Education’s Background Screening Clearinghouse. In accordance with House Bill 531, employment is contingent upon an applicant’s eligibility for clearance and the successful completion of all required background screenings prior to hire.
 For additional information about the background screening process, please visit: https://info.flclearinghouse.com

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job. 

  • Prepares, cooks, and serves food to students in accordance with menus and nutritional guidelines.
  • Handles and stores food safely, including checking and maintaining proper temperatures in accordance with food safety regulations.
  • Operates and maintains food warmers, serving stations, and other kitchen equipment, ensuring compliance with temperature and sanitation standards.
  • Upholds the highest standards of safety, cleanliness, and sanitation in all aspects of food preparation and service.
  • Monitors the condition of food service equipment and reports required maintenance or necessary repairs to supervisor. 
  • Sets up and cleans the cafeteria and serving areas before and after meal periods.
  • Cleans and sanitizes dishes, appliances, and all areas within the food service area.
  • Maintains inventory of food and supplies; assists in receiving, organizing, and storing deliveries and restocking inventory as needed.
  • Communicates effectively with students, staff, and supervisors to ensure smooth daily operations and a positive dining experience.
  • Attends vocational classes, seminars, and related in service training opportunities as assigned. 
  • Performs other duties as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • High School Diploma or GED equivalent preferred.
Experience:
  • None; food service experience preferred.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Food Safety Certification.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Ability to interact positively with students and perform duties with consistent courtesy and tact
  • Working knowledge of the English language.
  • Ability to communicate effectively.
  • Ability to understand and follow oral and written instructions.
  • Knowledge of the methods, supplies, equipment, and operating procedures related to food service.
  • Knowledge of safety precautions applicable to food handling and storage.
  • Ability to use independent judgement in relatively routine and stable situations.
  • Ability to work under stressful conditions as necessary.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with students, colleagues, and others.
  • General knowledge of reporting and record keeping principles and techniques.

GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

Under the general supervision of the Superintendent or designated supervisor, the Media Coordinator maintains website content and supports digital communications across all four Oasis Charter Schools, ensuring information is accurate, current, and accessible in accordance with established accessibility requirements and Cape Coral Charter School Authority (CCCSA) policies and procedures. The position also assists designated staff in maintaining book and media inventory records and reviewing materials for age and developmental appropriateness in accordance with Florida Department of Education guidelines and school policies and procedures. Performs related work as required.

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job. 

  • Posts, reviews, and updates website content for the Cape Coral Charter School Authority (CCCSA) and all Oasis Charter Schools, including news, announcements, calendars, staff information, and required notices, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and timely publication.
  • Reviews and corrects website content for accessibility, including alternative text, heading structure, color contrast, descriptive links, and captions, in accordance with established accessibility requirements.
  • Creates, converts, or remediates PDFs and other electronic documents into accessible formats, correcting document structure, reading order, tags, and formatting as needed.
  • Conducts regular website reviews for outdated information, broken links, and accessibility issues; documents findings, completes routine corrections, and coordinates unresolved technical issues with designated staff or the website platform vendor.
  • Maintains shared electronic files of approved images, documents, forms, and permission slips, ensuring current versions are available for publication and staff use.
  • Collects, reconciles, and maintains electronic inventories of books and media across all four schools, including classroom collections, and coordinates updates with designated school staff to screen books and media for age and developmental appropriateness using established Florida Department of Education guidelines and Charter School Authority procedures.
  • Maintains records of materials reviewed, authorized decisions, additions, and removals; prepares and publishes required collection and reading lists as directed.
  • Monitors school social media accounts in accordance with established posting expectations, communication procedures, and accessibility requirements.
  • Trains and supports staff throughout administration and all schools on routine website content updates, accessibility practices, document preparation, and established media procedures, as directed.
  • Maintains spreadsheets, review logs, and a calendar of recurring updates and reviews; tracks deadlines, approvals, corrections, and unresolved items and follows up with responsible staff.
  • May be assigned to back up other media or clerical staff after appropriate training.
  • Provides support in library/media centers and other learning facilities when appropriate.
  • Maintains confidentiality and complies with laws and policies concerning student information and school records.
  • Participates in training programs when appropriate.
  • Performs other duties as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • High school diploma or GED required. Sixty (60) hours of college credit from an accredited institution or Paraprofessional Certification required.
Experience:
  • Three (3) or more years of experience in an educational setting preferred.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Willingness to complete job-related accessibility training (such as through IAAP, DHS, The A11Y Collective, or an equivalent provider) within twelve (12) months of hire required.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • General knowledge of report and recordkeeping principles and techniques.
  • General knowledge of ADA, WCAG, and accessible document practices, or the ability to learn them quickly.
  • Skilled in written and oral communication for effective expression and clarity.
  • Ability to utilize a variety of modern office equipment and software, including content management systems, Microsoft Office, PDF tools, and social media platforms.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with supervisors, teachers, administrators, and staff across multiple campuses.
  • Ability to organize and review work for efficient results, accuracy, and attention to detail.
  • Ability to meet deadlines, manage multiple priorities, and work independently.
  • Ability to perform duties with consistent courtesy and tact in the best interest of the Cape Coral Charter School Authority (CCCSA).
  • Ability to issue and follow oral and written instructions.

Job.JobTitle: Oasis Charter Schools- High School Interventionist
Job.JobDescription:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

The Interventionist Teacher provides targeted small-group instruction, individualized academic interventions, and progress monitoring for students who demonstrate the greatest academic need. Working under the direction of the Principal or designee, the teacher uses assessment data to identify specific learning gaps, develop intervention plans, and adjust instruction to improve student growth and progress toward grade-level standards. The position expands the school’s capacity to provide timely academic support and helps classroom teachers meet the needs of all students.

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job.

  • Identifies and prioritizes students for intervention using multiple sources of information, including diagnostic and screening assessments, state and local assessments, classroom performance, teacher referrals, and the school’s Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) process.
  • Develops individualized intervention plans that document baseline performance, specific skill needs, measurable goals, instructional strategies, frequency and duration of services, progress-monitoring methods, and review dates.
  • Provides scheduled, evidence-based small-group and individualized instruction in assigned academic areas, which may include literacy, mathematics, foundational skills, course-specific prerequisite skills, and other areas identified through school data and student need, emphasizing the prerequisite and essential skills needed to access grade-level coursework and standards. Adapts instruction and materials to the developmental needs of the grade levels served.
  • Uses explicit instruction, modeling, guided practice, repeated opportunities for skill application, and timely, specific feedback to address identified learning gaps.
  • Organizes flexible instructional groups and coordinates intervention schedules with the Principal and classroom teachers to provide consistent services while supporting access to core instruction.
  • Prepares and implements intervention lesson plans and instructional activities aligned with identified skill deficits, applicable Florida academic standards, charter-approved curriculum, and approved intervention resources.
  • Administers approved diagnostic and progress-monitoring assessments at intervals established in intervention plans; analyzes results and adjusts instructional strategies, grouping, intensity, or duration based on student response.
  • Supports students in improving academic performance and, at the secondary level, course completion, credit attainment, and progress toward graduation requirements, as applicable to assigned grade levels, interventions, and student needs.
  • Maintains accurate, timely records of intervention plans, services delivered, attendance, assessment results, and student progress.
  • Collaborates regularly with classroom teachers to align intervention with classroom instruction, review specific learning gaps, share effective strategies, and support application of skills in classroom assignments.
  • Participates in MTSS, student support, and data review meetings; contributes documented evidence to decisions about continuing, modifying, intensifying, or exiting interventions.
  • Coordinates with exceptional student education staff, Section 504 coordinators, English language learner staff, counselors, and other appropriate personnel to support students’ identified needs and implement applicable accommodations within assigned responsibilities. This position does not assume ESE case-management, IEP development, Section 504 plan development, evaluation, or other compliance responsibilities unless separately assigned and appropriately qualified.
  • Communicates intervention goals and progress to students, families, classroom teachers, and administrators; helps students understand their learning goals and develop productive academic habits.
  • Establishes a safe, supportive, and structured learning environment that encourages participation, persistence, and student confidence.
  • Works with Administration to establish and review measures of position effectiveness, including growth from baseline, progress toward grade-level standards and individual goals, intervention participation, and relevant course performance and academic indicators; provides periodic summaries of student outcomes and intervention implementation, including students served, planned and delivered services, goal attainment, and recommendations for improvement, reviewed in the context of students’ starting points, needs, and participation.
  • Uses charter-approved instructional technology, assessment platforms, student information systems, learning management systems, and communication tools to support instruction, document services, and monitor student progress.
  • Provides appropriate supervision of students during assigned instructional periods and follows charter school policies and procedures related to student safety, emergency response, discipline, and mandatory reporting.
  • Attends and participates in required faculty meetings, professional learning communities related to instruction at assigned grade levels, academic intervention, assessment, and data analysis; uses feedback and results to improve practice.
  • Attends parent/guardian conferences, school events, and other assigned duties in accordance with the school calendar and charter school policies.
  • Maintains confidentiality, follows professional standards, and complies with applicable charter school policies and student support requirements.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in education or related field.
Experience:
  • Required: Previous teaching experience.
  • Preferred: Teaching or intervention experience at the assigned grade levels, and experience providing targeted academic intervention, using assessment data to guide instruction, and monitoring student progress.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Valid Florida teaching certificate appropriate to the assigned grade levels, subjects, and courses. Must maintain any additional certifications, endorsements, or training required for assigned intervention services, including applicable reading requirements.
  • Must meet applicable employment screening and fingerprinting requirements.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Knowledge of Florida academic standards, curriculum for assigned grade levels, and prerequisite and foundational skills in assigned instructional areas.
  • Knowledge of evidence-based intervention, explicit instruction, differentiated instruction, child and adolescent development and learning, and MTSS problem-solving processes.
  • Skill in identifying learning gaps, establishing measurable goals, and using diagnostic and progress-monitoring data to adjust instruction.
  • Ability to provide effective small-group and individualized instruction to students with varied academic, language, cultural, and learning needs.
  • Ability to align interventions with core instruction and collaborate effectively with classroom teachers and student support personnel.
  • Skill in organizing intervention schedules, maintaining accurate records, and using instructional technology and approved student data systems.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with students, families, and colleagues; provide constructive feedback; and maintain professional judgment and confidentiality.

Job.JobTitle: Oasis Charter Schools- High School English Teacher
Job.JobDescription:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

Under the general supervision of the Principal or designated supervisor, the Teacher is responsible for developing and implementing instructional lessons for secondary students in accordance with federal and state laws, as well as Charter School Authority guidelines. This position supports the effective operation of the school by coordinating and communicating with administrators, instructional and support staff, parents, and students. The role requires the ability to prioritize tasks and work independently, with periodic supervision or review. 

Background Screening Requirement:
Florida law requires all school personnel to undergo a Level 2 background screening through the Florida Department of Education’s Background Screening Clearinghouse. In accordance with House Bill 531, employment is contingent upon an applicant’s eligibility for clearance and the successful completion of all required background screenings prior to hire.
 For additional information about the background screening process, please visit: https://info.flclearinghouse.com

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job. 

  • Guides secondary students toward achieving their intellectual, emotional, physical, and social potential in a safe, inclusive, and efficient learning environment aligned with the goals of the school.
  • Plans and delivers instruction, both individually or cooperatively, that meet the individual needs, interests, and abilities of all students.
  • Contributes to the development, implementation, and evaluation of department or grade-level curriculum goals and instructional objectives.
  • Establishes a classroom environment that is safe, inclusive, and conducive to learning and appropriate to the maturity and interests of the students, fostering a culture of curiosity, participation, and mutual respect. 
  • Aligns instruction with curriculum goals by setting and clearly communicating objectives for lessons, units, and projects.
  • Utilizes a variety of instructional methods, materials, and resources appropriate for meeting student needs and learning objectives consistent with the capabilities of all individuals or student groups involved.
  • Effectively integrates technology to enhance instruction, student engagement, and academic outcomes.
  • Grades tests, exams, assignments, and projects; evaluates student performance and identifies learning strengths and challenges, Provides additional support when needed, and seeks support from specialists as appropriate.
  • Regularly monitors and assesses student progress, providing timely and constructive feedback to students and communicating academic performance, challenges, and achievements to parents or guardians.
  • Maintains open, consistent, and professional communication with colleagues, students, and parents or guardians to support student growth and academic success. 
  • Supports the implementation of school policies governing student conduct and promotes positive behavior and a respectful, well-managed classroom by developing fair and consistent rules and procedures to minimize disruptions and de-escalate students with social, emotional, and behavioral needs.
  • Recognizes and appropriately responds to signs of student distress or abuse in accordance with school procedures and law.
  • Plans and supervises meaningful tasks for auxiliary personnel and participates in evaluating their effectiveness in collaboration with department or grade-level leaders.
  • Maintains accurate, complete, and timely records in accordance with laws, Charter School Authority policies, and administrative regulations.
  • Participates in staff meetings, school committees, and other collaborative initiatives; collaborates with colleagues on interdisciplinary projects and instructional improvements.
  • Engages in ongoing professional development to maintain professional licensure and certifications and remain current with educational trends and best practices.
  • Promotes positive relationships and communication with colleagues, students, parents or guardians, and community members to enhance engagement and support student success.
  • Adheres to the Code of Ethics of the Education Profession in Florida and complies with all school and Charter School Authority policy requirements.
  • Promotes a culture of high performance and continuous improvement by modeling a commitment to excellence and lifelong learning.
  • Assists with school-related activities outside the classroom, including field trips, fundraisers, before and after school duties, and lunch or hall monitoring as assigned.
  • Performs other duties as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university.
Experience:
  • Three (3) years of related work experience.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Valid Florida teaching certificate covering appropriate area of responsibility.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • Knowledge of and experience with industry-standard computer applications.
  • Ability to work with diverse groups of people.
  • Ability to work effectively under the stress of deadlines, volume of workload, and multitasking requirements.
  • Ability to organize self, prioritize tasks, and maintain a high level of energy in a fast-paced environment to provide efficient services.
  • Bilingual skills are encouraged.

Job.JobTitle: Plans Examiner II, III - Plumbing / Mechanical / Development Services / Building
Job.JobDescription:
GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

SAFETY SENSITIVE:  No                          FINGERPRINTING REQUIRED:  Yes

About Us
The City of Cape Coral is the seventh largest city in Florida, has over 1,500 full-time employees, provides various career path opportunities, and offers a robust training and development program for improving current talents, developing new skills, and building effective business relationships.
 
Perks and Benefits

  • Free city-paid employee health coverage, additional for spouse or family
  • City Employee Health & Wellness Center for healthcare services
  • 5 weeks Paid Time Off (sick & vacation)
  • 11 paid holidays
  • Pension plan 
  • City-paid life and long-term disability insurance
  • Optional Vision and Dental Plans
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Gym membership reimbursement
  • And much more!

Minimum Qualifications

  • High School Diploma/GED.
  • Five (5) years of experience in construction industry design, plan review, and inspection field duties.
  • Must possess a valid state driver's license and obtain a valid Florida driver's license within thirty (30) days of hire or promotion.
  • Plans Examiner II ($67,308.80 Min - $105,372.80 Max) - One (1) Plans Examiner license issued by the Department of Business and Professional Regulations and one (1) Plans Examiner or Building Inspector license issued by the Department of Business and Professional Regulations, any discipline the area of which is determined by business need. 
  • Plans Examiner III ($70,699.20 Min - $110,635.20 Max) - One (1) Plans Examiner license issued by the Department of Business and Professional Regulations and two (2) or more Plans Examiner or Building Inspector licenses issued by the Department of Business and Professional Regulations, any discipline the area of which is determined by business need

 Preferred Qualifications

  • Current State of Florida Mechanical Inspector, Mechanical Plans Examiner, Plumbing Inspector, or Plumbing Plans Examiner certification; or equivalent ICC certification with the ability to obtain Florida certification through reciprocity preferred.
  • A minimum of two (2) years of experience actively performing plumbing and/or mechanical inspections and/or plan review services for a local jurisdiction, private provider, or similar code enforcement entity preferred.
  • Dual certification in both the plumbing and mechanical disciplines preferred.

Key Responsibilities

  • Reviews residential, commercial, and miscellaneous construction and project plans for the Department of Community Development.
  • Position provides support for Building or Development Services and maintains necessary certifications according to division of assignment.
  • Employees in this class are responsible for ensuring compliance with established standard building, fire and/or zoning codes and regulations.
  • Incumbents possess a broad background in general construction practices that provides solid knowledge of inspecting structures, reviewing plans, and interpreting various forms of site documentation, i.e., architectural drawings, maps, schematics, engineering designs.
  • Position is responsible for review and approval/denial of various permits, and the accurate recording of all approved permits.
  • Other related duties.

Please review the full job description by clicking on the link below.  To apply for the position, close the job description window and then click on the "Apply" button to complete your application.

PLANS EXAMINER PROVISIONAL, I, II, III JOB DESCRIPTION
 
An Equal Opportunity Employer and Drugfree Workplace

GENERAL STATEMENT OF JOB

**NOTE** 
This posting is intended to create a general candidate pool for substitute teacher opportunities across all schools. Applicants should not expect an immediate response after applying. When a substitute need arises, individual schools may review candidates from this applicant pool and contact those whose qualifications meet the needs of the position to schedule an interview.

Under general supervision of the Principal or designated supervisor, the Substitute Teacher is responsible for ensuring the continuation of learning in the absence of the regular classroom teacher.

Background Screening Requirement:
Florida law requires all school personnel to undergo a Level 2 background screening through the Florida Department of Education’s Background Screening Clearinghouse. In accordance with House Bill 531, employment is contingent upon an applicant’s eligibility for clearance and the successful completion of all required background screenings prior to hire.
For additional information about the background screening process, please visit: https://info.flclearinghouse.com

SPECIFIC DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Since every duty associated with this position may not be described herein, employees may be required to perform duties not specifically spelled out but may be considered incidental in the performance of this job. 

  • Reports to the principal or designee upon arrival to the school and reviews written expectations set by the school.
  • Maintains student behavior in class by supporting school policies governing student conduct and promoting positive behavior and a respectful, well-managed classroom.
  • Maintains the established routines and ensures a classroom environment that is safe, inclusive, and conducive to learning and appropriate to the maturity and interests of the students, fostering a culture of curiosity, participation, and mutual respect.
  • Delivers instruction based on the lesson plan provided utilizing a variety of instructional methods, materials, and resources appropriate for meeting student needs and learning objectives.
  • Consults with the principal or designee for approval prior to initiating any procedures not specified in the lesson plans provided and substitute teacher's handbook.
  • Reports to Principal or designee at the end of the day to verify whether or not   attendance is required on the following teaching day.
  • Adheres to the Code of Ethics of the Education Profession in Florida and complies with all school and Charter School Authority policy requirements to which regular teachers are subject and which good practice dictates.
  • Promotes a culture of high performance and continuous improvement by modeling a commitment to excellence and lifelong learning.
  • Assists with school-related activities outside the classroom, including field trips, fundraisers, before and after school duties, and lunch or hall monitoring as assigned.
  • Performs other duties as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Alternatives to the minimum qualifications can be made by the Board as they find appropriate and acceptable.
Education:

  • Associate’s degree from an accredited college or university.
  • Bachelor’s Degree Preferred
Experience:
  • Educational background preferred.
Licenses and Certifications:
  • Valid Florida teaching certificate preferred.

ADDITIONAL MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED: KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Skilled in oral communications for effective expression and clarity.
  • Some knowledge of report and record keeping principles and techniques and experience with industry-standard computer applications.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective-working relationships with supervisors, support staff, and others.
  • Ability to organize and review work for efficient results and accuracy.
  • Ability to handle a multitude of diverse tasks simultaneously while maintaining an attention to detail for the purpose of ensuring accuracy in task performance.
